16.en: We fought for their Greater Good, saw the benefit, and saw the cost. Now we are stuck here, surrounded by malignance and darkness. The only good left is for us to survive and return home, whatever the cost.

36.en: are a group of Kroot stranded in the Macharian Sector.

44.en: They are luring voidships into traps, ambushing them, killing everyone on board, and salvaging what tech and supplies they can.

52.en: Their goal is to survive and repair their warsphere. Then, leave the Macharian Sector behind for good and return to @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#tau-empire]{T’au Empire} space.

64.en: : The kinband’s crash site can be tucked away on a frontier or feral world, but could just as easily be hiding within debris fields and wreckage belts in a place like @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.rwTMhBwRA6wCOgIA]{Arrian’s Wrath} or the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.MzIWAwZ8jPAOydDi]{Sargassum Reaches}.

70.en: In the Macharian Sector’s salvage fields, strewn with destroyed voidships and orbiting junk, prospectors and salvage crews are disappearing. The culprits are a substantial kinband of Kroot from a crashed warsphere known as the

74.en: . Led by the flesh shaper @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor}, the kinband is stealing salvage, spare parts, and supplies from those they lure and ambush before disappearing quickly into the wilds, leaving none alive to tell the tale.

84.en: After being struck down by @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari} pirates while scouting the Macharian Sector, they aim to survive and get the

88.en: void-worthy again. But the pace of their repairs has been slow, their supplies are dwindling every day, and the kinband continues to take heavy losses. Each raid costs them more warriors, who were already thinned dramatically by the crash of the warsphere.

92.en: The longer they linger, the more likely they are to be discovered. Recently, @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.brh2O5CexxurRbM7.JournalEntryPage.YFKg8L1rfWbScqkr#ordo-hereticus]{Ordo Hereticus} acolytes were investigating the area, looking for an escaped rogue psyker. Both fell afoul of the kinband and were consumed, their voidships stripped for parts and scuttled, left as hulks waiting to lure the next group of investigators.

96.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is cunning, like most shapers. He will not press his luck and attack a much larger force than he has prepared to face. Nor will he give away the location of the crashed warsphere and the rest of the kinband if he can help it.

100.en: His losses are weighing on him, though, and with each new raid, he carefully weighs their options. He prefers to outnumber his enemies two to one at a minimum; he will not throw away precious Kroot lives for an obvious lost cause.

104.en: But he would push the kinband further if the opportunity arose to harvest parts from a Warp travel-capable voidship. He knows that if he can salvage from such a vessel instead of the shuttles and other smaller craft they regularly trap, the chances of finding what they need to complete the repairs to the

112.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is also not beyond talking to achieve what he needs. He prefers to be the first to strike in any conflict, but if someone attempts to engage him in dialogue, he will take a moment to listen. He is not above doing mercenary work for Imperial assets if it means avoiding punishment for the damage the kinband has already done and the parts they need fix to their warsphere.

120.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor's} kinband are down to a few dozen @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0Sws6uyhkY2nx4Go]{Kroot Carnivores} and @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.8EOYNULRU7nA8acm]{Kroot Mercenaries}. He is the last remaining flesh shaper among them. They have plenty of salvaged weapons, their own Kroot weaponry, and nearly three scores of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.15cqsEnrFd3vBoSA]{Kroot Hounds}. Their ship can be powered up, though it generally remains dormant so that it is not detected. Within the crashed ship, the decks are a mishmash of Kroot construction, with Imperial machinery used to repair the superstructure and most vital systems. Though there is no guarantee the two technological systems can be made compatible, Kroot philosophy encourages taking the strength of others and making it one's own. They have a pair of salvaged shuttles they use to travel to nearby areas and hunting grounds.

124.en: Besides the weapons they carry, the kinband has gathered a lot of useless salvage. They aim to barter it, especially for more materials to fix the warsphere. Initiating a bargain with them will be difficult for any characters since the kinband’s first reaction will be to try and eat them. A Silent Trader has made this work, but they have no exclusive deal. While the trader is only interested in xenos tech, the kinband has quite a stockpile of Imperial tech in which they have very little interest.

132.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor's} plan has worked well so far, so the kinband sees little need to deviate from it. The kinband attacks vessels that arrive to salvage the existing debris. They consume the crew, salvage what they can, and then use the new wreckage to draw in others to try and attack them. Sometimes they set off a distress signal to ensure another ship arrives but are sure to leave only the most recent signal running.

142.en: Members of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor}’s Kinband have consumed the flesh of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial citizens} and some @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.xxcZ1PUz0t1ycevK.JournalEntryPage.GyAY9bnCmCZ3JjzK#drukhari]{Drukhari}. They have gained the following modification:

150.en: : The Kroot have consumed hyper-aware creatures, allowing them to detect movements within Medium Range with Advantage and potentially reveal hidden creatures.

160.en: A Silent Trader is feeding @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} information on happenings in the system in return for scraps of xenotech the kinband has salvaged. The trader refuses to provide them direct aid to fix the warsphere. If the warsphere is repaired, the kinband will leave the system for good, which does the trader no good. However, the trader is weak-willed, and if Inquisitorial agents press them, giving up the kinband’s location may be their best leverage.

164.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.0PaBk1ctcf5eQRbC]{Nar’itor} is concerned about some of the modifications a few of his band have started to exhibit. It is subtle, but he fears that some of the flesh they have consumed is beginning to lead their strand toward an evolutionary dead end. The last thing he wants is for them is to finally be freed, only to discover he has guided the kinband into extinction.
